thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Priority 1 network alert for az-12-eu (timestamp=1815004321). High tail latency and connection failures observed for IPv6 traffic to our public ingress. Possible PMTUD failure / ICMPv6 filtering. Links: https://internal.ops/alerts/1815004321

mike_oncall: acked. I'm on it, grabbing logs and looking at per-AZ egress. @sara you able to pull recent customer reports?

sara: jess-support sent a few customer threads — uploads + large websocket reconnects failing over v6, fallback to v4 succeeding. Example: cust-acme-prod in EU saw 504s after ~15s.

trent-netops: I'm seeing a spike in ICMPv6 "Packet too big" counters being dropped at the edge LB. Cloud-side WAF has a rate limit rule that started firing ~00:08 UTC.

alice-eng: reproducing from a test VM in eu-west-3: ping -s 1600 to our ingress IP over v6 -> no reply. tcpdump on host shows SYN from client, SYN-ACK from server, then no Path MTU 'Packet too big' ICMPv6 reaching client.

jess-support: multiple customers report only large payloads failing. Small requests ok. Seems like only >1500 byte paths affected.

mike_oncall: ok hypothesis: Cloud provider is rate-limiting ICMPv6 Type 2 (Packet Too Big) for that AZ edge pool, so PMTUD can't discover smaller MTU. Results: connections stall on large payloads. Immediate mitigations we can do: 1) add TCPMSS clamp on egress/loadbalancer path, 2) ask cloud-sre to whitelist ICMPv6 PTB for our edge subnets, 3) temporarily prefer IPv4 for customer-facing routes. I'll start 1 & 3.

trent-netops: starting ip6tables TCPMSS clamp on proxy fleet (canary 5% then full). Command: 
```
# on proxy nodes
ip6tables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
```
Rolling to 5% now.

cloud-sre: reached out to cloud provider support (ticket CP-84721). They acknowledge WAF rule tripped due to increased ICMPv6 rate from certain upstream routers and temporarily applied aggressive dropping. They're reviewing.

mike_oncall: can we also enable kernel level MTU probing on our proxies while we wait? 
```
# enable on linux
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1
sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_ra=1
```
Note: tcp_mtu_probing only impacts TCP over IPv4; we still need ip6tables clamp for IPv6.

sara: customer comms: telling affected customers we have a mitigation in progress and recommending IPv4 as a fallback for now. No ETA yet.

alice-eng: can confirm canary looks good: 5% proxy fleet with clamp shows restored large payload uploads in synthetic test. Metrics: upstream 200s increased from 78%->98% success on canary.

jess-support: keeping a running list of affected accounts — will prioritize any on Dedicated plans. Adding contact in case provider escalates.

mike_oncall: rolling clamp to 100% now. Monitoring ingress error-rate and p50/p95 latency.

(5 minutes pass)

trent-netops: clamp rolled to 100%. Ingress 5xx for large payloads down ~92% in az-12. Cloud provider reopened their rule and will exempt our subnets for ICMPv6 PTB. They estimate full propagation in ~20min.

cloud-sre: provider confirmed whitelist applied. Please keep an eye on edge WAF logs for any regressions. Ticket CP-84721 updated and assigned to network security team.

mike_oncall: starting to revert IPv6->IPv4 preference change after provider whitelist propagated. Will keep clamp for now until postmortem.

jess-support: customers notified of temporary fix and that we're monitoring; some asked for timeline for permanent fix.

alice-eng: quick note for permanent remediation: we should (A) request explicit allow for ICMPv6 PTB with provider, (B) add global ip6tables tcpmss clamp as a default on proxies, (C) add test to our e2e to detect PTB filtering in each AZ (simple large-pkt path check). I'll file tasks.

mike_oncall: handing to @sara for follow-up and postmortem. Summary for handoff: root cause = Cloud WAF rate-limiting ICMPv6 PTB in az-12 causing PMTUD failures for IPv6 flows with path MTU > 1500. Mitigations applied: ip6tables TCPMSS clamp (temporary), tcp_mtu_probing on Linux, provider whitelist for PTB, temporary IPv4 preference for critical routes. Impact: 4% of customer requests in az-12 (large payloads over IPv6) experienced failures for ~18 minutes.

sara: taking over. Creating incident write-up and postmortem ticket PM-1815004321. Assigning action items to eng, netops, and cloud-sre. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

mike_oncall: cleared from on-call at 1815004920.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident channel will remain open for follow-up tasks and postmortem.

sara: final note for SOC/compliance: no evidence of malicious activity — this appears to be an overzealous rate-limit. We'll include provider log excerpts in the postmortem.

alice-eng: queued changelist to keep TCPMSS clamp permanent on proxy config and to add e2e detection. PR: https://internal.code/redwood/ops/merge/3245

jess-support: closing customer follow-ups as mitigated where verified. Will reopen if they see regression.

sara: closing thread for incident operations. Postmortem draft expected in 48h.
